sps.title: Commission Implementing Regulation amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072 as regards measures to prevent the entry into the Union territory, and the spread within it, of Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Agrilus planipennis, Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, Raspberry leaf curl virus, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, Strawberry leaf curl virus, Thaumatotibia leucotreta, Toumeyella parvicornis and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticola, as regards changes of protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora, amending Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 and repealing Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1927
sps.description:
Implementing Regulation 2019/2072 contains the list of Union quarantine pests, protected zone quarantine pests, and regulated non-quarantine pests (RNQPs). Furthermore, it lays down phytosanitary requirements for import and internal movement of plants, plant products and other objects that may pose a phytosanitary risk to the European Union.

This draft amendment of Implementing Regulation 2019/2072:

  • Delists Aleurocanthus spiniferus, Raspberry leaf curl virus, and Strawberry leaf curl virus as quarantine pests and repeals measures associated with these pests.
  • Lists the following species as quarantine pests and sets, where applicable, measures to avoid their entry and spread in the Union territory: Chloridea virescens, Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense Tropical Race 4, Spodoptera ornithogalli, Spodoptera praefica, and Xanthomonas citri pv. viticola. 

Please note that Chloridea virescens and Spodoptera ornithogalli were already listed in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2022/1941 as species that are not to be introduced into, moved within, held, multiplied or released in the Union territory.

  • Updates  requirements for import and internal movement, including addition/revision of the respective CN codes, for Agrilus planipennis, Hirschmanniella spp., Meloidogyne enterolobii, and Thaumatotibia leucotreta.
  • Lists Toumeyella parvicornis as regulated non-quarantine pest and sets measure to avoid its spread in the Union.
  • Introduces changes to the protected zones in relation to Beet necrotic yellow vein virus and Erwinia amylovora.

Clarifies and corrects some inconsistencies (e.g. change of scientific names).

sps.title: Notice of Administration Order of Saudi Food and Drug Authority Ref. No. 16506 dated 25 October 2026 entitled “Temporary ban on importation of poultry meat, eggs and their products originating from Wielkopolskie in Poland”
sps.description: Following the WOAH report dated 19 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Wielkopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Wielkopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

sps.title: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
sps.description:
Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/SPS/N/TUR/126 on 20/06/2022. 

The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:

 

Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: 13 October 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonized with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.

 

•    The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.

•    E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.

•    For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.

•    E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.

•     E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.

•    The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some traditional fermented alcoholic beverages produced in the EU.

•    E 334 Tartaric acid (L(+)-), E 335 Sodium tartrates, E 336 Potassium tartrates, E 337 Sodium potassium tartrate, and E 354 Calcium tartrate have been removed from Group I and are now permitted only in specific categories with specified maximum usage levels. Their use in food enzymes and flavourings has also been restricted in Annex III.

•    In the “16. Desserts” food category, the scope of use for E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate has been expanded to include water-based gelatine-based desserts.

•    The scope of use for E 460 Cellulose powder and E 575 Glucono-delta-lactone has been expanded to permit their use in unripened soft spreadable cheese products within the “01.7.6 Cheese products” food category.

•    In the “04.1.1 Whole fresh fruits and vegetables” food category, the authorization for surface applications of E 471 mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids and E 903 carnauba wax for glazing purposes has been extended to include passion fruit, kiwi, and cassava. E 322 Lecithins and E 570 Fatty acids have been authorized under Annex III as carriers in preparations intended for polishing cassava.

•    E 960b Steviol glycosides produced by fermentation have been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This amendment includes E 960b in the existing “E 960a–960d: Steviol glycosides” group, allowing this sweetener to be used under the same conditions as other steviol glycosides.

•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the authorization for the use of E 466 sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (cellulose gum) has been revoked.

•    In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the use of E 301 sodium ascorbate has been authorized in microencapsulated vitamin A preparations used in infant and follow-on formulas.

•     In Annex III, Section 1, the scope of use for E 1202 polyvinylpyrrolidone has been expanded to permit its use as a carrier in colouring tablets intended for the decorative colouring of eggshells.

•     In the food category “16. Desserts; excluding products falling under categories 1, 3, and 4,” the use of E 200–202 sorbic acid—potassium sorbate is permitted only in unheated plant-based mousses.

•    The use of E 999 Quillaia extract is permitted in both solid and liquid food supplements (Categories 17.1 and 17.2). Additionally, provisions have been added to Annex III to allow its use as an emulsifier in flavourings.

•     E 412 guar gum has been banned in the “13.1.1 Infant formula” food category.

•    The following additions have been made to the list of food categories under Section D of Annex II:

          •    18.1 Processed foods not covered by Categories 18.2 and 18.3, excluding foods for infants and young children

          •   18.2 Meal-replacement foods intended for weight loss

          •   18.3 Foods specifically manufactured to reduce the gluten content of gluten-containing ingredients or to substitute gluten-containing ingredients

•    The following food categories listed under Annex II, SECTION D have been deleted. Authority over these categories lies with the Ministry of Health:

         •    13.1.4 Special medical-purpose dietary foods for infants and young children, as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Special Medical-Purpose Dietary Foods / Special formulas for infants

         •   13.1.4.1 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for newborns and special formulas for newborns

         •    3.1.4.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for infants and young children as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes

         •   13.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes as defined in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes (excluding those listed in category (13.1.4))

•    E 942 The sale of nitrous oxide to the end consumer is prohibited.

•   The phrase “Non-alcoholic wine-like products” has been removed from the name of the food category “14.2.2 Turkish Food Codex – Wine Regulation: Wine and Other Products.”

•    In the subcategories under the “08. Meat” category, the definition has been used instead of the word “sausage.” The term “sausage” (sausages) is used in EU countries to refer to meat products served in casings and is not limited to the narrower meaning used in Türkiye.

•    To prevent the uncontrolled use of sorbic acid and benzoates, which may be present due to carry over from ingredients in meatless çiğ köfte products, under the category “12.7 Salads and savoury/spiced spreads for sandwiches,” the following limits have been established for meatless çiğ köfte: E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate; E 210-113 Benzoic acid—benzoates at a maximum usage level of 200 mg/kg for each additive group. 

•     In the “14.1.1 Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Fruit Juices and Similar Products,” pickle brine has been excluded from the list of foods in the “Fruit Juices and Vegetable Juices” category where Group I food additives may be used. The use of E 210–213 (benzoic acid—benzoates) is permitted at a maximum level of 200 mg/l.

•    Additional restrictions have been introduced in Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Türkiye and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products.”

         •    In sucuk: water-holding agents in the E 400–469 range, E 235 natamycin, and E 553b talc are prohibited.

         •    In heat-treated sucuk, the following are prohibited: E 400–469, E 235 natamycin, E 243 ethyl laurol arginate, and E 553b talc.

         •    In pastırma, raw or cooked döner, poultry döner, and raw or cooked meatballs and poultry meatballs, E 400–469 are prohibited.

         •    All additives are prohibited in ground meat kavurma.

•    In Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Our Country and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products,” certain food additives are exempt from these restrictions.

         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in çiğ köfte, meatless çiğ köfte, and mezze (such as haydari, Arnavut liver, fava beans, shakshuka, hummus, and similar dishes), E 267 (buffered vinegar) is exempt from this prohibition.

         •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in köme, pestil, bastık, walnut-stuffed sucuk, and similar products, as well as in baklava, E 330 citric acid is exempt from this prohibition.

 

This Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication with a transitional period as 31 December 2028. Products placed on the market before 31 December 2028 by food businesses operating before the publication date of the Regulation establishing this article, and foods containing these products, may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life.

sps.title: Administrative Regulation No. 27/2026 Amendment to Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food"
sps.description:
To further safeguard public health, enhance the efficiency of risk management, and promote harmonization between local regulations and international standards, the Macao Special Administrative Region Government has amended Administrative Regulation No. 23/2018 “Maximum Limits of Heavy Metal Contaminants in Food". This amendment is based on the latest standards recommended by the Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC), as well as those  established by major food-supplying countries and regions. This regulation has been scrutinized through risk assessment to ensure that it adequately protect public health in Macao, China.

The revised regulation establishes a total of 165 maximum limits (MLs) for specified heavy metal contaminants in specific food items, of which 92 MLs represent optimizations or new additions. 
A reasonable transition period of approximately 6 months will be granted following the official promulgation of the regulation. This will provide sufficient time for the food industry to adapt its importation and safety control processes, and for local testing laboratories to establish and validate the necessary analytical capabilities in accordance with the new requirements.

sps.title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. …, issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: “Flavoured Milk” (No. 3)
sps.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk" (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.

The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection.

sps.title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. …, issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No. 3)
sps.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. ... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk" (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.

a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.

b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.

c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk"  to align with the raw materials used.

sps.title:
Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (England) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/1197);

Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (Scotland) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products (Scotland) Regulations 2012; 

Declaration of special measures: importation of certain products from certain third countries and territories (Wales) - The Trade in Animals and Related Products (Wales) Regulations 2011 (SI 2011/2379 (w. 252))
sps.description:
These declarations of special measures are necessary to prevent the incursion of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) to the United Kingdom. 

The measures prohibit the import of hay and straw and certain animal by-products from animals susceptible to foot-and-mouth disease from any countries, or zones within countries, that are not recognised by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) as free of foot-and-mouth disease – either with or without vaccination. This is in line with the recommendations set down in Articles 8.8.28, 8.8.30, 8.8.32, 8.8.33 and 8.8.36-8.8.40 of the WOAH Terrestrial Code.

The prohibition does not apply to animal by-products if they are an intermediate product, a trade sample or research and diagnostic samples.

sps.title: Notice of Administration Order of Saudi Food and Drug Authority Ref. No. 16506 dated 25 October 2026 entitled “Temporary ban on importation of poultry meat, eggs and their products originating from Wielkopolskie in Poland”
sps.description: Following the WOAH report dated 19 October 2026, a Newcastle virus outbreak has occurred in Wielkopolskie in Poland. In compliance with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), Terrestrial Animal Health Code Chapter 10.9, it is deemed necessary for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to prevent the entry of the HPAI virus into the country. Therefore, the import of poultry meat, eggs and their products from Wielkopolskie in Poland to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is temporarily suspended (with the exception of processed poultry meat and egg products exposed to either heat or other treatments that ensure deactivation of the Newcastle virus, as long as it conforms with the approved health requirements, and standards, with a health certificate issued by the official bodies in Poland prove that the product is free from the virus).

tbt.title: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents.
tbt.description:
FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions.  

FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
tbt.productsFreeText: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions.
tbt.objectivesFreeText:
Diet plays an important role in overall health and wellbeing. Poor diet can contribute to overweight and obesity and increase the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases. Around two-thirds of the Australian and New Zealand population are currently overweight or obese, and an estimated 15% of deaths in Australasia are attributable to dietary risks. National dietary guidelines emphasise the importance of choosing a variety of nutritious foods and limiting foods high in saturated fat, sugars and sodium.

 

The Health Star Rating (HSR) system is a front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPL) scheme that summarises a food’s overall nutritional profile using a simple star rating. Evidence indicates tools such as FoPL, used alongside other broader public health strategies, can improve consumer understanding of the healthfulness of foods and support healthier choices, with interpretive summary indicators like the HSR system generally performing favourably compared to other FoPL systems.

 

The objective of the HSR system is to provide a quick, easy, standardised way for consumers to compare the nutritional value of similar foods to help them make informed healthier food choices in-line with dietary guidelines.

 

Most consumers agree the HSR symbol makes it easier to identify healthier foods, and a majority report using the system at least sometimes when shopping. However, even though the system has been implemented on a voluntary basis for over 10 years, low uptake and selective use of the system by industry have limited effective consumer use.

 

The objective of this proposal is to consider requiring the HSR symbol on foods for sale in Australia and New Zealand to better support healthier food choices and thereby contribute to broader public health efforts to reduce the prevalence of overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases in Australia and New Zealand.

tbt.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk " (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.

The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection.

tbt.title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. ...., issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No.3)
tbt.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk " (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.

a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.

b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.

c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk"  to align with the raw materials used.

tbt.title: Law of Ukraine  of 13 October 2026 No. 5013 “On Amendments to the Tax Code of Ukraine and Certain Other Laws of Ukraine Regarding the Postponement of the Introduction of Electronic Traceability of the Circulation of Alcoholic Beverages, Tobacco Products and Liquids Used in Electronic Cigarettes”
tbt.description:
The Law amends the Tax Code of Ukraine and certain other laws to postpone the introduction of the electronic traceability system of the circulation of alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes.

The Law postpones the introduction of the electronic excise stamp system from 1 November 2026 to 1 July 2027. It provides for the electronic traceability system to operate in test mode until 30 June 2027 and in full operation from 1 July 2027.

The Law establishes transitional arrangements for the registration of economic operators in the electronic system, the circulation of products bearing paper excise stamps and the application of financial penalties during the transition period. It sets specific deadlines for the registration of economic operators, including 1 April 2027 for operators holding the relevant licences as of 1 January 2027.

The Law also provides that alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes manufactured in Ukraine or imported into Ukraine before 1 July 2027 and bearing paper excise stamps may remain in circulation until 31 December 2028, inclusive. Their circulation is governed by the legislation applicable before 1 July 2027 concerning products bearing paper excise stamps, without applying the requirements of the Tax Code of Ukraine and the relevant Law concerning the operation of the electronic system.

Alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes imported into Ukraine from 1 July 2027 are to be marked with graphic elements of electronic excise stamps in accordance with the procedure established by law.

Consultation paper (16 pages) on policy options to regulate e-bike safety and survey (18 pages).

You can access the consultation paper and survey on the ACCC’s Consultation Hub.
tbt_all.description:
The ACCC is consulting on options for a mandatory safety standard for electrically power-assisted cycles, commonly known as e-bikes and associated devices, including conversion kits and tampering devices, and e-bike batteries and chargers.

E-bikes are bicycles fitted with electric motors to provide power-assistance to riders and are intended to be primarily powered by peddling. E-bike conversion kits consist of a motor, battery and other components that convert conventional pedal bicycles into e-bikes. Tampering devices are products that allow modification to an e-bikes power output and speed.

The popularity of e-bikes has grown significantly in recent years, and these devices provide many community benefits. However, fires, injuries and deaths related to e-bikes have also increased and is of significant concern.

We are consulting on options for a mandatory safety standard to address the risks posed by e-bikes and associated devices, while maintaining the benefits e-bikes provide.

A mandatory safety standard could apply minimum safety requirements or restrictions to the supply of e-bikes and associated devices.

This consultation seeks views on the introduction of a mandatory safety standard for e‑bikes, including the scope and application.

Draft Unsafe Goods (Consumer Sand Products) Notice 2026 (6 pages, in English), https://www.mbie.govt.nz/have-your-say/consultation-on-draft-unsafe-goods-consumer-sand-products-notice-2026.

The final notice has been issued by the Minister of Commerce and Consumer Affairs under section 31 of the Fair Trading Act 1986. The notice declares certain toys containing sand and decorative, craft or artistic goods containing accessible sand to be unsafe goods unless prescribed asbestos testing requirements have been met. The notice incorporates by reference:

  • ISO 22262-2:2026, Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 2: Quantitative determination of asbestos by gravimetric and microscopical methods (50 pages, in English);
  • ISO 22262-2:2014, Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 2: Quantitative determination of asbestos by gravimetric and microscopical methods (47 pages, in English);
  • ISO 22262-1:2012 Air quality — Bulk materials — Part 1: Sampling and qualitative determination of asbestos in commercial bulk materials (70 pages, in English.
tbt_all.description: Since November 2025, New Zealand suppliers have undertaken 23 recalls of consumer sand products following the detection of asbestos contamination, affecting approximately 46,000 units. Research has demonstrated that asbestos fibres may become airborne during normal use of some sand products, creating a risk of inhalation and associated adverse health effects. The proposed measure seeks to prevent the supply of asbestos-contaminated consumer sand products in New Zealand. The use of an internationally recognised testing method and laboratory accreditation requirements intend to provide a consistent and reliable basis for demonstrating compliance. The measure is intended as an interim requirement pending development of longer-term product safety regulation addressing asbestos contamination in consumer sand products (hence the urgency).

tbt_all.description:
To reduce GHG emissions from the use of Hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) refrigerants in the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning (RAC) sector, NEA will introduce limits on the Global Warming Potential (GWP) of refrigerants to restrict the import and supply of equipment using refrigerants with high GWP. 

 

Since 2022, NEA has imposed GWP limits for household air-conditioners, refrigerators and water-cooled chillers used for large building cooling systems.

 

The Environmental Protection and Management (Prescribed Regulated Goods) Order 2022 and Environmental Protection and Management (Regulated Goods and Registered Suppliers) Regulation 2022 will be amended to:

  1. Introduce GWP limit of 150 for refrigerants used in centralised commercial refrigeration systems, with effect from 1 July 2027.
  2. Introduce GWP limit of 150 for refrigerants used in passenger cabin air-conditioning systems in Motor Vehicles (i.e. passenger cars/taxis and light goods vehicles), with effect from 1 July 2028.
     

The GWP limits apply only to newly supplied equipment. 

 

Details of the restrictions are available on NEA’s website at: https://www.nea.gov.sg/our-services/climate-change-energy-efficiency/climate-change/reducing-ghg-emissions-from-the-use-of-refrigerants-in-rac-sector

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing a final rule to update the incorporation by reference of several voluntary consensus standards in the Agency's formaldehyde standards for composite wood products regulations under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) due to the standards having been updated or superseded by the issuing organizations. These new standards primarily update test methods and product standards concerning composite wood products that use formaldehyde. EPA is also conforming these updated standards in the scope and definitional sections in the final rule and incorporating by reference a new small scale quality control chamber test method, similar to current methods already incorporated by reference. EPA is also removing one standard that was previously incorporated by reference to avoid redundancy, given that another identical, internationally recognized version of the standard is already incorporated by reference in this rule.

 

This final rule is effective on 27 November 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain material listed in the rule is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 27 November 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain other material listed in the rule was approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 10 February 2017, 7 February 2018, 21 August 2019, and 23 March 2023.

tbt_all.title: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review
tbt_all.description:
Proposed rule - The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Source Category to address additional concerns raised with prior regulatory amendments finalized in March 2024. Specifically, the EPA is proposing changes in response to certain petitions for reconsideration of the March 2024 amendments, changes based on policy decisions and supporting legal interpretations, and changes that correct and clarify the regulatory text of the new source performance standards and emission guidelines. First, the EPA proposes to rescind the Super Emitter Program. Second, the EPA proposes to subcategorize different types of well sites affected and designated facilities to address issues related to the requirements finalized in March 2024 for marginal well sites and conventional well sites. Third, the EPA proposes changes to address issues related to liquids unloading, process controllers, pumps, fugitive emissions, storage vessels, covers and closed vent systems, equipment leaks at gas plants, and associated gas. Fourth, the EPA proposes changes to certain requirements finalized in March 2024 related to control devices and to provide owners and operators the option to conduct optical gas imaging surveys according to Appendix K for gas processing facilities. Lastly, the EPA proposes changes to correct inadvertent errors and to clarify regulatory language.

 

EPA will hold a virtual public hearing starting at 10am Eastern Time on 16 November 2026 for the Proposed Reconsideration of the 2024 Final Clean Air Act Rule. Pre-registration is now open. If you would like to provide testimony at the public hearing, please register at https://survey.alchemer.com/s3/9078544/OG-Recon2-PublicHearing-2026.  For any questions or concerns, please contact the public hearing team at OG-Recon2-PublicHearing-2026@rti.org.

tbt_all.title: Draft Decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of Government Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP dated 29 June 2025 detailing a number of articles and prescribing measures for organizing and guiding the implementation of the Law on Pharmacy
tbt_all.description:
The draft Decree contains the following provisions:
6.1. Amendments to reduce and simplify administrative procedures:
- Implementation of the plan to reduce and simplify administrative procedures relating to production and business activities under Resolution No. 66.16/2026/NQ-CP.
- Implementation of the plan to reduce and simplify administrative procedures based on data under Resolution No. 66.7/NQ-CP.
6.2. Guidance on the amendments and additions to the Law on Pharmacy proposed in the draft Law amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Law on Children, the Law on Persons with Disabilities, the Law on Medical Examination and Treatment, the Law on Pharmacy, the Law on the Elderly and the Law on Health Insurance, to align the entry into force of the Decree with that of the amending Law:
- Implementation of the plan to decentralize the administrative procedure for issuing Certificates of Confirmation of Drug Advertising Content by authorizing provincial-level People's Committees to process applications and issue these certificates, which would be valid nationwide.
- Amendments and additions to provisions on the publication and republication of proposed wholesale drug prices in Articles 114, 119 and 130, and addition of Article 115a on the procedures for receiving submissions for such publication and republication; provisions specifying which drugs may have their proposed wholesale prices published after the first batch has been sold on the market; procedures for submitting recommendations concerning published or republished proposed wholesale drug prices; and responsibilities for sharing data on drugs, medicinal raw materials cleared through customs for export or import, including drug import prices, for regulatory purposes.
6.3. Provisions to address practical issues requiring immediate resolution during the implementation of Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP:
- Amendments and additions to Article 21 to provide for publication of information on the list of pharmacies in a pharmacy chain after the establishment organizing the pharmacy chain has been granted a Certificate of Eligibility for Pharmaceutical Business.
- Amendment and supplementation of the title of Article 70 by adding the phrase “semi-finished drugs for export”.
- Amendments and additions to Articles 78 and 82 to cover drugs for State health program where the drug provider has been designated in a decision of the Minister of Health approving the contractor selection arrangements for a procurement package involving purchases through international organizations under the special-case contractor selection procedure prescribed by the law on bidding; establishments conducting pharmaceutical activities for non-commercial purposes would also be authorized to import such drugs.
- Amendments and additions to Article 85 to cover internal transfers within medical examination and treatment establishments.
- Amendments and additions to Article 96 to allow a Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) inspection report from the competent inspecting authority to be replaced by a GMP inspection report from a Stringent Regulatory Authority (SRA), or a pharmaceutical regulatory authority recognized by the Ministry of Health on the basis of the World Health Organization (WHO) classification, or a report of a GMP inspection conducted by WHO under its Prequalification Program; the requirement to submit an “updated Site Master File” would be waived for foreign manufacturing establishments assessed on the basis of recognition or mutual recognition under Article 94. The amendment would also clarify the responsibilities of registration applicants and manufacturing establishments, as well as establishments that look up the documents specified in Clause 5 of Article 96 and use the information obtained from them.
- Amendments and additions concerning format and presentation to ensure clarity and transparency and prevent differing interpretations of legal provisions.
- Amendments and additions to certain forms in the Appendices to Decree No. 163/2025/ND-CP to align them with the amendments and additions in the draft Decree.

tbt_all.title: Proposal P1067 – Health Star Rating System: 2nd Call for Submissions and Supporting Documents.
tbt_all.description:
FSANZ has prepared a proposed draft amendment to the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (the Code) to mandate the display of a Health Star Rating (HSR) symbol on food for sale in Australia and New Zealand. The 2nd call for submissions provides FSANZ’s assessment and the proposed draft amendment, which would require the HSR to be calculated using a prescribed algorithm and the HSR symbol to be displayed on the front of most packaged foods for retail sale that are required to bear a nutrition information panel, subject to specified exemptions and prohibitions.  

FSANZ seeks submissions on the proposed regulatory approach to inform its final assessment and a decision on whether to approve, amend or reject the proposed draft amendment.
tbt_all.productsFreeText: Imported and domestically produced packaged foods for retail sale in Australia and New Zealand that are required to bear a label, subject to certain exemptions and prohibitions.
tbt_all.objectivesFreeText:
Diet plays an important role in overall health and wellbeing. Poor diet can contribute to overweight and obesity and increase the risk of diet-related non-communicable diseases. Around two-thirds of the Australian and New Zealand population are currently overweight or obese, and an estimated 15% of deaths in Australasia are attributable to dietary risks. National dietary guidelines emphasise the importance of choosing a variety of nutritious foods and limiting foods high in saturated fat, sugars and sodium.

 

The Health Star Rating (HSR) system is a front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPL) scheme that summarises a food’s overall nutritional profile using a simple star rating. Evidence indicates tools such as FoPL, used alongside other broader public health strategies, can improve consumer understanding of the healthfulness of foods and support healthier choices, with interpretive summary indicators like the HSR system generally performing favourably compared to other FoPL systems.

 

The objective of the HSR system is to provide a quick, easy, standardised way for consumers to compare the nutritional value of similar foods to help them make informed healthier food choices in-line with dietary guidelines.

 

Most consumers agree the HSR symbol makes it easier to identify healthier foods, and a majority report using the system at least sometimes when shopping. However, even though the system has been implemented on a voluntary basis for over 10 years, low uptake and selective use of the system by industry have limited effective consumer use.

 

The objective of this proposal is to consider requiring the HSR symbol on foods for sale in Australia and New Zealand to better support healthier food choices and thereby contribute to broader public health efforts to reduce the prevalence of overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases in Australia and New Zealand.

tbt_all.title: Draft Decree amending and supplementing a number of articles of the Decrees in the field of manufacturing, assembling and importing road motor vehicles and the Decree detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law, amending and supplementing: Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP on conditions for manufacturing, assembling, importing and warranty and maintenance service business of automobiles; Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP on inspection and certification of quality, technical safety and environmental protection of imported automobiles and imported components under international treaties to which Vietnam is a party; and Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law
tbt_all.description:
The draft Decree amends and supplements a number of articles of Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP dated 17 October 2017 (as amended and supplemented by Decrees No. 17/2020/NĐ-CP, No. 14/2026/NĐ-CP and No. 117/2026/NĐ-CP), Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP dated 16 August 2023 (as amended and supplemented by Decree No. 14/2026/NĐ-CP), and Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP dated 14 January 2026 of the Government.
The draft Decree applies to enterprises manufacturing, assembling and importing automobiles in Vietnam, as well as relevant agencies, organizations and individuals. 
Its main contents are as follows:
1. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 116/2017/NĐ-CP (Chapter I)
The draft Decree provides amendments and supplements to the government’s Decree no. 116/2017/ND-CP stipulating conditions for the manufacture, assembly, and import of automobiles, and the provision of automobile warranty and maintenance services (as amended and supplemented by Decree no. 17/2020/ND-CP dated February 5, 2020; Decree no. 14/2026/ND-CP dated January 13, 2026; and Decree no. 117/2026/ND-CP dated April 3, 2026) (referred to as Decree no. 116/2017/ND-CP, which stipulates the conditions for automobile manufacturing, assembly and importation, removing the business of automobile warranty and maintenance services from its scope of regulation.
2. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP on the inspection and certification of imported automobiles (Chapter II)
The draft Decree provides amendments and supplements to the government’s Decree no. 60/2023/ND-CP dated august 16, 2023, regarding the inspection and certification of technical safety quality and environmental protection for imported automobiles and components in accordance with international treaties to which Viet Nam is a party (as amended and supplemented by the government’s Decree no. 14/2026/ND-CP) 
In the draft Decree, Appendix VI attached to Decree No. 60/2023/NĐ-CP shall be replaced by Appendix I attached to the draft Decree.
3. Amendments and supplements to Decree No. 16/2026/NĐ-CP detailing a number of articles of the Railway Law (Chapter III)
In the draft Decree, Clause 1 of Article 26 and Clause 1 of Article 35 are repealed.

tbt_all.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: "Flavoured Milk " (No. 3) amends the labelling requirements for name designations of flavoured milk.

The main objective is to revise and clarify the food name designations on the label for flavoured milk produced from milk powder or other milk components (such as whey, casein, lactose, or other recombined milk solids). The label must explicitly declare statements indicating the use of milk powder or recombined milk components as part of the food name (e.g., "obtained from milk powder" or "obtained from recombining separated components of cow's milk"). This amendment aims to ensure that consumers receive accurate and transparent information on product labels and to enhance consumer protection.

tbt_all.title: Draft MOPH Notification (No. …) B.E. ...., issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 (1979) Re: “Cow’s Milk” (No.3)
tbt_all.description:
This draft notification of the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH) (No. …) B.E. .... issued by virtue of the Food Act B.E. 2522 Re: "Cow’s Milk " (No. 3) amends the definitions of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk", as well as the name designations of these food products.

a. Amend the definition of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" to clarify that it is drawn exclusively from the cow, and include additional processing methods to comprehensively cover current practices, such as sterilization and UHT.

b. Amend the definition of "recombined milk" to explicitly state that it is produced from milk powder or by recombining separated cow’s milk components, such as whey, casein, and lactose, and add requirements specifying that the quality or standards of recombined milk shall be equivalent to those of fresh plain fluid cow's milk or plain fluid cow's milk.

c. Amend the name designations of "fresh plain fluid cow's milk" and "recombined milk"  to align with the raw materials used.

tbt_all.title: Law of Ukraine  of 13 October 2026 No. 5013 “On Amendments to the Tax Code of Ukraine and Certain Other Laws of Ukraine Regarding the Postponement of the Introduction of Electronic Traceability of the Circulation of Alcoholic Beverages, Tobacco Products and Liquids Used in Electronic Cigarettes”
tbt_all.description:
The Law amends the Tax Code of Ukraine and certain other laws to postpone the introduction of the electronic traceability system of the circulation of alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes.

The Law postpones the introduction of the electronic excise stamp system from 1 November 2026 to 1 July 2027. It provides for the electronic traceability system to operate in test mode until 30 June 2027 and in full operation from 1 July 2027.

The Law establishes transitional arrangements for the registration of economic operators in the electronic system, the circulation of products bearing paper excise stamps and the application of financial penalties during the transition period. It sets specific deadlines for the registration of economic operators, including 1 April 2027 for operators holding the relevant licences as of 1 January 2027.

The Law also provides that alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes manufactured in Ukraine or imported into Ukraine before 1 July 2027 and bearing paper excise stamps may remain in circulation until 31 December 2028, inclusive. Their circulation is governed by the legislation applicable before 1 July 2027 concerning products bearing paper excise stamps, without applying the requirements of the Tax Code of Ukraine and the relevant Law concerning the operation of the electronic system.

Alcoholic beverages, tobacco products and liquids used in electronic cigarettes imported into Ukraine from 1 July 2027 are to be marked with graphic elements of electronic excise stamps in accordance with the procedure established by law.

tbt_all.title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerning the non-renewal of the approval of the active substance phenmedipham in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 of the European Parliament and of the Council, and amending Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 540/2011
tbt_all.description:
This draft Commission Implementing Regulation provides that the approval of the active substance phenmedipham is not renewed in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. Member States shall withdraw authorisations for plant protection products containing phenmedipham as an active substance. The non-renewal of approval is based on the first evaluation of the substance for use as a pesticide active substance in the EU under Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009. The substance was formerly assessed and approved under Directive 91/414/ EEC.

This decision only concerns the placing on the market of this substance and plant protection products containing it. Following non-approval and the expiry of all grace periods for stocks of products containing this substance, separate action will be taken on MRLs and a separate notification will be made in accordance with SPS procedures.

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)
Protection of animal or plant life or health (TBT)

tbt_all.objectivesFreeText:
In order for an active substance to be approved in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 (concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market), it must be demonstrated that the substance is not harmful to human health, animal health or the environment. Criteria are listed in Article 4 of the Regulation (and also detailed in Annex II thereto) which must be met to enable approval. 

During the evaluation and peer-review of phenmedipham, two critical areas of concerns and several areas that could not be finalised were identified. These are detailed in the conclusion of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA): phenmedipham meets the criteria to be identified as an endocrine disruptor for the T-modality for non-target organisms other than mammals and effects at population level cannot be excluded and the technical specifications proposed by both applicants are not covered by the batches used in the key toxicological studies. In addition, several parts of the risk assessment could not be finalised by EFSA, including the consumer risk assessment via dietary intake and the risk assessment to aquatic organisms (algae). The outcome of the risk assessment, as documented in the EFSA Conclusion, identifies twenty-one data gaps. Although the applicant, when commenting on the EFSA Conclusion, indicated that thirteen of the twenty-one data gaps could be solved in applications for the renewal of product authorisations at Member State level, this is not possible because at least one safe use must be identified at the approval level (as confirmed by the ECJ in its recent judgement in case C-316/24 P on cypermethrin). 

These concerns mean that phenmedipham does not meet the approval criteria as outlined in Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 and therefore, the approval of phenmedipham should not be renewed for the use in plant protection products.

Existing authorisations will need to be withdrawn; Member States must withdraw existing plant protection products containing phenmedipham at the latest by 6 months from the date of entry into force. A period of grace in line with Article 46 of Regulation 1107/2009 is allowed for and shall expire at the latest 12 months from the entry into force (allowing for a final season of use).

tbt_all.title: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Announces Upper C-Band Clearinghouse Selection Criteria and Submission Process
tbt_all.description:
In this document, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) announces that it has received detailed selection criteria and related submission instructions for proposals for the position of Upper C-band Clearinghouse. In Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band, GN Docket Nos. 25-59 and 18- 122, Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46 (24 July 2026) (Upper C-band R&O), the Commission provided for the creation of an independent, third-party Upper C-band Clearinghouse to oversee the cost-related aspects of the Upper C-band transition, including the receipt, review, and disposition of all actual cost and lump sum reimbursement claims. The Upper C-band Clearinghouse will also administer the rebates for adjacent band radio altimeter retrofits.

 

Potential clearinghouse candidates must email the selection committee with any questions about the selection criteria or submission requirements no later than 23 October 2026. Potential clearinghouse candidates must submit proposals according to the filing instructions contained in the selection committee's notification no later than 9 November 2026.

tbt_all.title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
tbt_all.description: Notice of proposed rulemaking - The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, ''Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment.'' The proposed updates to the standard are intended to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety. The first two proposed changes would amend the test voltage specification for integral beam type headlamps and remove requirements that apply to vertical headlamp arrangements. Further proposed changes address vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls. Those modifications would limit the application of certain requirements for manually operated turn signal, hazard warning signal, and beam switching controls to vehicles with manually operated driving controls. The changes are intended to address regulatory burdens and costs associated with equipment that does not fulfill the same purpose or provide safety benefits in an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls as in a vehicle with such controls. The changes would also narrow certain requirements for telltales to vehicles with manually operated driving controls and incorporate the term ''telltale'' where appropriate throughout the standard. Finally, a proposed addition to the standard would allow cyan-colored ADS marker lamps as optional motor vehicle lighting equipment in ADS-equipped vehicles.

tbt_all.title: Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper (Annex Decree)
tbt_all.description:
Viet Nam informs WTO Members that the Ministry of Industry and Trade adopted Circular No. 62/2026/TT-BCT dated 30 September 2026 promulgating Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper. The Circular will enter into force on 15 November 2026.

The draft measure was previously notified in G/TBT/N/VNM/429 Amendment 09:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT National technical regulation for towel paper and toilet tissue paper.

This addendum notifies the adoption and availability of the final text. The adoption date above replaces the proposed adoption dates in the previous notifications.

 

Scope & Definitions: Clarifies the definition of tissue paper (including large-roll tissue paper intended for further processing).

 

Technical Requirements & Chemicals: Updates requirements for chemical management during production, mandating compliance with the Law on Chemicals No. 69/2025/QH15.

 

Product Labeling: Labeling must be carried out in accordance with Decree No. 37/2026/NĐ-CP, which provides guidelines for the Law on Product and Goods Quality.

 

Conformity Assessment & Certification:

- Declaration of conformity must follow either Method 5 or Method 7, as stipulated in Circular 14/2026/TT-BKHCN.

- A certificate of conformity issued under Method 5 shall be valid for no more than 3 years.

- Assessments are based on certification results from an accredited certification body, or on self-assessment results derived from testing conducted by an accredited/designated laboratory.

Update of Testing Standards (Test Methods): Incorporates and references the latest equivalent international standards (ISO/EN) for physical and mechanical properties.The notified final documents are Circular No. 62/2026/TT-BCT (2 pages) and Amendment 01:2026 QCVN 09:2015/BCT (7 pages), in Vietnamese. The complete final text is attached and is available at the link provided above.

 

Responsible agency: Ministry of Industry and Trade.

 

Technical contact: Viet Nam Industry Agency, 54 Hai Ba Trung Street, Cua Nam Ward, Ha Noi, Viet Nam. Mr Duong Xuan Dieu; telephone: +84 912 215 854; email: dieudx@moit.gov.vn.

tbt_all.title: Draft Commission Implementing Regulation laying down rules for the application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards access to and use of certain information in the battery passport
tbt_all.description: This draft Commission Implementing Regulation concerns the parts of the EU battery passport for which access is not public, but restricted to persons with a legitimate interest. It specifies which persons are to be considered persons with a legitimate interest (e.g. repairers and recyclers), to which information listed in the battery passport they shall have access, and to what extent they can download, share, publish and re-use that information.
tbt_all.productsFreeText: Industrial batteries, including residential battery energy storage systems; electric vehicle batteries; batteries for light means of transport
tbt_all.objectivesFreeText: Reliable information regarding batteries is essential for their repair, repurposing, remanufacturing, recycling and for deciding between these actions. Being able to make informed choices on the further life and treatment of batteries allows to make the best environmental choice. Some of the necessary information may, however, contain information that is commercially sensitive to the battery manufacturer. Therefore, it is necessary to restrict who can have access to such information and what they can do with it, as already envisaged under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 in notification G/TBT/N/EU/775.

tbt_all.description:
In response to a request from the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (Auto Innovators), the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is announcing a 30-day extension of the public comment period for the Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) published on 22 September 2026 (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2043/Add.2). The SNPRM supplements NHTSA's September 2023 notice of proposed rulemaking (notified as G/TBT/N/USA/2043) to amend NHTSA's regulations to include an advanced crash test dummy (the Test Device for Human Occupant Restraint (THOR) 50th percentile adult male) by requesting comment on specifying an additional spine configuration and an alternative to the face foam, and announcing the availability of additional documents. The comment period for the SNPRM was originally scheduled to end on 22 October 2026. It will now end on 21 November 2026.

 

The comment period for the SNPRM published on 22 September 2026 at 91 FR 60068 is extended to 21 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 66827, 23 October 2026, Title 49 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 572:

https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-23/pdf/2026-21730.pdf

 

This extension of comment period and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/2043 are identified by Docket Number NHTSA-2023-0031. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/NHTSA-2023-0031/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 21 November 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with the regulator and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.
